title: Pummeling
shortDefinition: Pummeling is the repeated battle to regain inside lanes with hands, head, knees, or hips.
whyItMatters: No-gi has no gi grips, so pummeling is how control is rebuilt after every reaction.
deepExplanation: Pummeling is not only underhook fighting. Guard retention has knee pummeling; leg locks have knee-line pummeling; front headlock defense has elbow and chin pummeling.
beginnerView: If you lose inside position, recover it before attacking.
advancedView: Pummel by reaction: where the opponent frames, another inside lane opens.

ifThenExamples.if: If you lose Pummeling during the exchange.
ifThenExamples.then: Stop accelerating, recover the nearest body structure, then continue the technique.
ifThenExamples.why: Modern no-gi punishes forceful continuation after structure is lost.

ifThenExamples.if: If the opponent correctly answers your first line.
ifThenExamples.then: Use Pummeling to switch to a safer branch instead of forcing the same line.
ifThenExamples.why: A good concept turns the opponent’s reaction into information for the next decision.

commonMisunderstandings.misunderstanding: Pummeling is a single technical trick.
commonMisunderstandings.correction: Treat it as a decision rule that appears across many positions.

commonMisunderstandings.misunderstanding: Understanding the concept automatically makes it work live.
commonMisunderstandings.correction: The concept needs body signals, short cues, and positional rolling.

trainingCues: Find the body signal instead of guessing generally.
If structure is lost, reset one layer first.
Drill slowly, then test with progressive resistance.
